definition: Renting computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking, software) over the internet, paying for what you use.
Security duties split between Microsoft and you. You always own your data, devices and identities.
Provider owns the hardware, anyone can use it, no CapEx.
Cloud used by one organisation. Full control, CapEx for the hardware.
Public and private cloud connected and used together.
Using more than one public cloud provider.
Up-front spend on physical infrastructure, such as buying servers.
Ongoing spend on services as you use them. Cloud spend is OpEx.
Pay only for what you use, no up-front cost.
Billed per use with no commitment.
Commit for 1 or 3 years in exchange for a big discount.
Spare Azure capacity, deeply discounted, can be evicted at any time.
Reuse your existing Windows Server or SQL Server licences on Azure.
No servers to manage. Code runs on events and you pay per execution.
Keeps a service running with minimal downtime. Measured as an SLA percentage.
Service level agreement: Microsoft's promised uptime, for example 99.9%.
Ability to handle more or less load by adding or removing resources.
Give a machine more CPU or RAM.
Add more machines or instances.
Scaling that happens automatically with demand.
Ability to recover from failures and keep working.
Steady performance and forecastable cost.
Rent the infrastructure. You manage the OS and up. Most control.
Microsoft runs the infrastructure and OS. You bring the app and data.
Finished software you just use. Least management.
Move existing servers to cloud VMs unchanged (IaaS).
Physical building of servers. Grouped into regions and zones.
Geographic area of one or more datacenters on a low-latency network.
Two regions in the same geography, at least 300 miles apart. Updated one at a time.
Isolated Azure for government or legal needs: Azure Government (US), Azure China (21Vianet).
Separate datacenter(s) in a region with their own power, cooling and network. At least 3 per region.
A single service instance: VM, storage account, VNet, database.
Logical container. Each resource is in exactly one. Groups can't nest. Deleting one deletes its contents.
Billing and access-control boundary that holds resource groups.
Container for subscriptions. Policy and RBAC set here are inherited. Up to 6 levels deep.
IaaS server in Azure with full OS control.
Identical, load-balanced VMs that autoscale.
Spreads VMs across fault domains (up to 3) and update domains (up to 20).
Group of hardware sharing power and network, like a rack.
Group of VMs rebooted together during maintenance.
Windows desktops and apps hosted in Azure, used from any device.
Lightweight, portable app package that shares the host OS.
Run a container fast without managing VMs.
Serverless containers with built-in scaling and load balancing.
Azure Kubernetes Service: managed container orchestration.
Serverless, event-driven code, billed per execution.
PaaS hosting for web apps, APIs and mobile back ends.
Your private network in Azure.
A smaller address range inside a VNet.
Private link between VNets over Microsoft's backbone.
Hosts DNS domains in Azure. Can't buy domain names there.
Encrypted tunnel over the internet: site-to-site, point-to-site, network-to-network.
Private connection to Azure through a provider, not over the internet.
Service reachable on a public IP address.
Network interface with a private IP in your VNet, linked to a service (Private Link).
Container for Azure Storage data with a globally unique name.
Unstructured object storage (images, video, backups).
Managed SMB/NFS file shares you can mount.
Messages (up to 64 KB) between app components.
NoSQL key/attribute storage.
Block storage volume for a VM.
Blob tiers from frequent to rare access. Minimum days: 0 / 30 / 90 / 180.
Moving an archived blob back online. Can take hours.
3 copies in one datacenter.
3 copies across 3 availability zones.
LRS plus a copy in a secondary region.
ZRS plus a copy in a secondary region.
Geo-redundant plus read access to the secondary at any time.
Command-line tool to copy data to and from storage.
Desktop GUI for managing storage.
Syncs Windows file servers with Azure Files and caches hot files.
Hub to discover, assess and migrate to Azure.
Physical device shipped to move large data offline.
Azure's cloud identity service (formerly Azure AD).
Managed domain join, LDAP, Kerberos and group policy without domain controllers.
Syncs on-prem Active Directory with Entra ID.
One sign-in for many apps.
Two or more factors: something you know, have or are.
Windows Hello for Business, Authenticator app, FIDO2 keys.
Outside users sign in with their own accounts (B2B, External ID).
If-then sign-in policies: signals lead to allow, require MFA or block.
Assign roles at a scope to control who can do what.
Full plus grant access / full minus grant access / view only.
Verify explicitly, use least privilege, assume breach.
Layers: physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application, data.
Security posture (secure score) and threat protection across Azure, on-prem and other clouds.
Data into Azure (generally free) / data out of Azure (charged).
Estimates the cost of services before you deploy.
Retired by Microsoft. Older practice tests still mention it. Use the pricing calculator.
Cost analysis, budgets and alerts on actual spending.
Name/value labels on resources for cost and organisation. Not inherited by default.
Discovers, classifies and governs data across your whole estate.
Enforces rules on resource properties and reports compliance.
A group of policies assigned together.
Can read and modify, can't delete.
Can read only: no changes, no deletes.
Web GUI for managing Azure.
Browser shell, already signed in, Bash or PowerShell.
Cross-platform az commands.
Az cmdlets such as New-AzVM.
Extends Azure management to on-prem and other clouds.
Defining infrastructure in code for repeatable deployments.
Deployment and management layer every request goes through.
Declarative JSON describing resources to deploy.
Simpler language that compiles to ARM JSON.
Recommendations: reliability, security, performance, operational excellence, cost.
Azure outages, maintenance and advisories affecting you.
Health of one of your resources.
Collects and analyses metrics and logs, and raises alerts.
Query tool for Azure Monitor logs (KQL).
Who and how to notify when an alert fires (email, SMS, webhook).
Performance monitoring for web apps.
In your own building or datacenter, not in the cloud.
Create and set up a resource so it is ready to use.
Put an app or resource into Azure so it runs.
An app or job that runs in the cloud.
Moving apps, servers or data to Azure.
An older app built for older technology. It often needs things like Kerberos or LDAP.
Running many virtual machines on one physical machine.
The software that creates and runs virtual machines.
A service where the provider runs the underlying parts for you.
The delay before data arrives. Lower is faster.
How much data can move per second over a connection.
How much data or work actually gets processed per second.
Spreading traffic across several servers so none is overloaded.
Time a service is working / time it is not.
A period when a service is down.
How much of the time a service is up, usually as a %.
Extra copies, so one failure doesn't lose anything.
How safe stored data is from being lost (the "nines", e.g. 11 nines).
The system keeps working even if one part fails.
Switching to a backup copy when the main one fails.
Getting systems back after a big failure, such as a region outage.
An area such as Europe that contains several regions. Data stays inside it.
Where data is physically stored, which matters for laws.
An address where a service can be reached (a URL or IP).
Scrambling data so only someone with the key can read it.
Data stored on disk / data moving over a network.
A software update that fixes bugs or security holes.
Your organisation's own instance of Microsoft Entra ID (its directory).
Who or what is signing in: a user, an app or a device.
Proving who you are, e.g. signing in with a password and MFA.
What you are allowed to do after signing in (RBAC decides this).
A user, group or app that can be given access.
Give only the access needed, nothing more.
The level a setting applies to: management group, subscription, resource group or resource.
Settings flow down from a parent level to everything below it.
Rules and control over how the cloud is used.
Meeting laws and standards (e.g. GDPR, ISO 27001).
Fixing something that breaks a rule, e.g. Azure Policy fixing non-compliant resources.
Data a system sends about itself, such as metrics and logs.
Numbers measured over time, such as CPU 75%.
Time-stamped records of events, such as "VM started at 09:02".
Automatically managing, scaling and restarting many containers or tasks.
You describe the end result you want, not the steps.
You give step-by-step commands.
Running it twice gives the same result as running it once.
A specific product size or edition you can buy, such as a VM size.
A level of a service, such as Basic, Standard or Premium, or Hot and Cool.
The maximum amount you are allowed to create.
Data going out of Azure (charged) / data coming in (free).
Allow and deny rules for traffic to a subnet or VM. Network layer.
Managed, stateful firewall that protects a whole virtual network. More powerful than an NSG.
Defends against floods of traffic meant to take you offline. Perimeter layer.
Spreads network traffic across VMs in a region.
Load balancer for web traffic (HTTP), with an optional web application firewall.
DNS-based routing that sends users to the best region.
Global entry point for web apps: fast routing, caching and a firewall.
Caches content on servers close to users so it loads faster.
Secure RDP/SSH into VMs from the portal, without giving them public IPs.
Safe storage for secrets, passwords, keys and certificates.
Cloud SIEM: collects security data and detects and responds to threats.
Managed relational SQL database (PaaS).
Globally distributed NoSQL database.
Managed open-source relational databases.
Low-code, serverless workflows that connect apps and services.
Backs up VMs, files and databases.
Replicates VMs to another region so you can fail over in a disaster.
Store of Microsoft and third-party solutions. Purchases may add cost.
Free credit and free services for a limited time to try Azure.
Microsoft guidance for good cloud design. Reliability is one of its pillars, and it shapes predictability.
Cutting waste: right-size, automate, monitor, optimise. Shut down what is idle.
Run your existing VMware workloads in Azure.
Commit to an hourly compute spend for 1 or 3 years. More flexible than a reservation.
Autoscale, templates, health monitoring and alerts.
Ways to manage it: portal, CLI, APIs, PowerShell.
The deployment types: public, private and hybrid (plus multicloud).
What you sign up with. It holds your subscriptions and is an identity in Entra ID.
12 months of popular products, a credit for the first 30 days, and some always-free services.
$100 credit, free services and developer tools, no credit card needed.
A Microsoft partner that sells Azure with managed-cloud solutions.
A subscription gets its own invoice.
Access policies are applied at the subscription level.
The single top-level management group in every Entra tenant.
Pinned to one availability zone you choose (VMs, managed disks).
Replicated across zones automatically (ZRS, SQL Database).
Always available from Azure geographies. Survives zone and region outages.
A template with an OS and tools used to create a VM.
B burstable, D general purpose, E memory, F compute, M large memory, L storage, N GPU.
Both PaaS. Container Apps add built-in load balancing and scaling.
Run a program or script alongside an App Service app, on a schedule or trigger.
The stateful kind of Azure Functions. Plain Functions are stateless.
Prebuilt AI through APIs: language, speech, vision, documents.
Generative AI such as chat and content generation, with security and governance controls.
Build, train and manage custom machine learning models.
Secure two-way communication between the cloud and IoT devices.
A simplified SaaS platform for IoT solutions.
Runs cloud workloads on devices close to where the data is created.
Lets a VNet reach Azure SQL or storage accounts securely, with optimal routing.
Rules that control where traffic is sent. UDR = user-defined route.
Border Gateway Protocol: shares routes between on-premises and Azure.
A specialised VM acting as a firewall or WAN optimiser.
Two VPN gateway types. Route-based is needed for VNet-to-VNet, point-to-site and multisite.
Links your on-premises sites through the Microsoft network, not the internet.
The private connection from your network to Microsoft through a provider.
An Azure DNS record that follows the target resource if its IP changes.
Premium account type for Azure Files. Supports both SMB and NFS.
Big-data analytics storage built on Blob storage.
Recovery point objective: how far behind the secondary copy can be. Typically under 15 minutes for Azure Storage.
Passwordless sign-in tied to your PC, with biometric or PIN.
Phone app. Passwordless with number matching plus biometric or PIN.
Hardware key for passwordless sign-in. Cannot be phished.
Partners sign in as guest users in your directory with their own accounts.
Mutual trust between tenants for Teams shared channels. No guest accounts.
Customer-facing identity. Formerly Azure AD B2C.
A regular check that guests and users still need their access.
Device management. Used for device-based Conditional Access.
Users reset their own passwords. An Entra ID feature.
Security guidance that Defender for Cloud recommendations follow.
Opens management ports only when needed. A Defender for Cloud feature.
Grouping of regions used for data-transfer pricing. Not an availability zone.
Cost Management view of spending by resource, region, billing cycle and so on.
A spending limit with alerts, and optionally automation.
Warns you when spending reaches a threshold.
Warns at 90% and 100% of an Azure Prepayment.
Enterprise Agreement alert when a department reaches part of its quota.
Microsoft portal for security, privacy and compliance documents and audit reports.
Azure Policy fixing non-compliant resources, such as adding a missing tag.
Marking a resource as exempt from a policy.
AI assistant for Azure operations. Always check its suggestions.
Global view of Azure health across all services and regions.
Application Insights synthetic requests that check your app responds.
The condition (metric or log) that triggers an Azure Monitor alert.
The path data takes through your systems. A Purview feature.
Labelling data by sensitivity. A Purview feature.
